tiles: 200+ weekly posts written, formatted, and published by an AI pipeline
Make.com orchestrates LLM writing, tagging, and CMS publishing
Hand-drawn iPad Pro illustrations, shipped as lightweight Lottie animations
Python migration scripts carried everything over to GitHub Pages
challenge: Running a blog that ships 200+ posts a week is impossible manually — that is more output than a small newsroom. The usual automated answer (mass AI content) reads sterile and hurts the brand more than no posts at all. So the real problem was twofold: build a pipeline that can actually publish at that volume, and make the output feel crafted instead of churned.
approach: I built a Make.com pipeline that triggers an LLM to draft each post, another model to tag and categorize it, and a publishing step that pushes it into Webflow's CMS on a schedule. On the design side, I drew hundreds of illustrations on iPad Pro, converted them through After Effects and Illustrator into Lottie animations (a format that stays tiny even when animated), and used custom line animations to guide the reader's eye between sections. When the whole thing migrated to GitHub Pages, Python utilities handled conditional visibility, external-link conversion, and collection-page generation.
result: The site publishes 200+ posts every week with no daily human touch, and it still looks like a designed magazine rather than an AI content farm. The Lottie approach kept page weight low despite heavy animation, and the same Make.com + LLM pattern now underpins several of the production pipelines I run for other projects.
